summary: SL-096 triaged the three red last-access tests as one environment fault. The engine's TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP sits where luafv moves a parent's last access when a child is opened with write access. Underneath it was one real defect: the scan's own child keep-open moved parents that LastAccessKept still counted as kept. The product change is a few lines in Scanner.CountListingOpen (Scanner.cs:332-347). The bulk of the diff is a TempTree redirect out of %SystemRoot%, deepest-first back-dating, five default-suite Facts that build in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests on purpose, and two fitness rules hardened with JSON corpora. The suite went from 692 to 789 and is green under both TEMPs.

payload.reason: Reflection on SL-096 written from the full record. All stages ran to a pass except reflect and commit. validate-slice #2 passed with O-015 still open.
payload.summary: SL-096 triaged the three red last-access tests as one environment fault. The product change is a few lines in Scanner.CountListingOpen (Scanner.cs:332-347). The bulk of the diff is a TempTree redirect out of %SystemRoot%, deepest-first back-dating, five default-suite Facts that build in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests on purpose, and two fitness rules hardened with JSON corpora. payload.estimate_error: Opened as medium size and medium risk, by a person. The product tier was about right: the behavioural fix is tiny and was measured before it was built. The size was understated. Accepting critique findings M1 and m2 as "close the class" turned a counter fix plus a redirect into guard-rail infrastructure, and the build record shows 20 files changed. The suite grew from 692 (survey) to 789 (build). At least 75 of the 97 new tests are corpus rows: the mutation runs show 34 rows in the route-corpus test and 41 in the skip-corpus test. The rest are the Windows-folder Facts, the TempTreeRootTests rows and a reflection check. The risk tier was right for a different reason than the design gave. The default suite now writes into a folder this user cannot list, and three stages leaked unrecoverable folders there while working. Rule 2 still shipped with six known spellings let through (SC-177).

learned.lesson: Before diagnosing any 'pre-existing' red test in this project, run the same filter twice: once with TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (the engine's inherited value) and once with TEMP set to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. This is the single most discriminating check. It explained three tests that stayed red through six SL-095 validations. A mismatch means the location is the cause, not DisableLastAccess=2, which reads ENABLED in both.
learned.evidence: Survey and investigation: 20/23 vs 23/23 on the LastAccessTests and HeldOpenTreeTests filter, and 689/692 vs 692/692 on FsAnalyser.slnx. fsutil printed 'DisableLastAccess = 2 (System Managed, Last Access Time Updates ENABLED)' in both runs.

learned.lesson: The TempTree redirect and fitness rule 2 guard only tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/**/*.cs. Everything else that reads the inherited TEMP still lands in C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, where children cannot be listed and Remove-Item is denied. That covers tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 (New-TempDir at :71, cleanups at :182 and :859), the engine's acceptance bug project and any new .ps1 probe. A slice that adds a fixture or probe outside Core.Tests must choose its own root and delete with [IO.Directory]::Delete.
learned.evidence: Code review ran RuleCases -Case C-003 under the engine TEMP: checks printed ok, then 'Access is denied' at :859 and exit 1, with the scratch folder left behind. C-001 exits 0. The bug test builds directly at C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-sl096-<guid> and is excluded from rule 2 and from TempTree.

learned.lesson: Loop stages leak folders into C:\Windows\Temp that nobody without admin rights can find. Only C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests is listable by this user, so a leftover check works only there. Any survey probe, review script or mutation re-run of the engine's bug test should root in C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests\<guid> or in the user's temp, and say so in its record.
learned.evidence: Survey left C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex> (certain). The code review's C-003 run probably left fsa-parity-case-<10 hex>. Validate re-ran the bug test twice for mutations A and B, and its cleanup is unverifiable ('not-run' in validate #2). All three are filed as person/admin work.

learned.lesson: After restoring a mutated source file, touch it or force a rebuild before reading the next result. A restore by Copy-Item or git checkout keeps the old timestamp, MSBuild skips the compile, and the DLL keeps the mutated code. A red right after a mutation run is first suspected to be this trap, not the fix. The design had already recorded this trap as a measured claim, yet the build's own script hit it. The engine's mutation runner in taad_v3 has no touch step.
learned.evidence: Spike 3 discarded runs c1-c3 as invalid. In the build, the bug test went red and the first full-suite attempt showed 3 failed until Scanner.cs was touched. The design's outside claim read 'Nothing breaks. The mutation check touches the file anyway.'

learned.lesson: When a critique finding is accepted as 'close the class', size the slice for a corpus, a test harness and a rule rewrite, not for the original one-line fix. In this repo that meant JSON corpus files fed by a Theory, SettledPatterns made internal, and fitness.yaml entries reformatted. A medium bug fix became 20 files and about +97 tests.
learned.evidence: Build record: 20 files changed, e885d7da8. Suite 692 to 789. LastAccessRuleCorpusTests has 34 route-rule rows and 41 skip-rule rows (mutation runs '4 of 34 failed' and '4 of 41 failed').

learned.lesson: Regexes that a critique proposes as the fix for a fitness-rule finding must be run against a corpus before they go to the builder. This repo writes paths in \\?\ extended form everywhere (LongPath.ToExtended, TempTree.ExtendedRoot, Scanner.IsAtOrUnder), and a pattern that requires a quote straight before the drive letter misses it. Seed any path-rule corpus with those spellings plus Path.Combine split arguments, the GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows, SpecialFolderOption.X) overload, and %SystemDrive%.
learned.evidence: M1's proposed Path.GetTempPath pattern was incomplete. m2's proposed `\[\s*Trait\s*\(` missed `[Fact, Trait(...)]`, `[TraitAttribute(...)]` and SkipWhen/SkipUnless, which the builder had to fix (corpus rows S18/S19, S27, S05). Code review round 2 then found six more spellings of the Windows Temp folder quiet against rule 2 (SC-177).

learned.lesson: A must-verify precondition that the design itself files for a person (a Windows 10 machine, writing to %ProgramData%, an administrator) cannot be discharged by any automated stage. Waive or file it at critique time. Left aimed at validate, it halted validate #1 and cost a second lap that learned nothing.
learned.evidence: O-015 was filed for a person in the design's filed_for_later and also raised as an obligation. validate-slice #1 halted 'O-015 aimed at this stage is still open'. validate #2 passed with O-015 still open, and the validator wrote 'A revalidation would learn nothing'.

learned.lesson: The kept-counter correction is coded for the whole Windows folder (Scanner.WindowsFolderFromEnvironment) but was measured only in %SystemRoot%\Temp. The Scanner class remarks (Scanner.cs:22-26) claim the move 'under the Windows folder' in general, while ScanResult.LastAccessKept states the limit precisely. A writable subfolder elsewhere under C:\Windows where luafv does not move the parent (luafv excludes some subdirectories) would under-count, and none of the == tests reach it.
learned.evidence: Code-review drift note on Scanner.cs:22-26. Real scans of C:\Windows\Web (asked 14, kept 0) and C:\Windows\Fonts (asked 1, kept 0) never populate the set, so no real input has exercised the correction outside Temp.

learned.lesson: Close waived findings at the end of the build if the same slice's structure fixed them. m7 was waived to SC-174, then the build made TempTree's root an instance field and Outside() build beside it, which is exactly m7's fix. The build left 'SC-174 can likely close' as prose, so the backlog still carries a done item.
learned.evidence: Build deviation note on the TempTree root, and its LEFT OPEN line 'SC-174 (m7) can likely close: TempTree.Outside() now builds under the root the tree was given'.

candidates.title: Root tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 scratch folders outside C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and delete them with [IO.Directory]::Delete
candidates.why: Review finding m1 was deferred with the reason that a later slice would cover it. The filed slice is 'route SyncRootRig/CloudRig through TempTree' and its text does not mention RuleCases, so the item can be lost. Measured by the code review: `RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-003` under TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP prints its checks ok, then throws 'Access is denied' at tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:859 (Remove-Item in the finally) and exits 1. It leaves C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\fsa-parity-case-<10 hex>, which this user cannot list or remove. Breakdown: New-TempDir at :71 uses [IO.Path]::GetTempPath(). The Remove-Item cleanups are at :182 and :859. C-001 exits 0 under both TEMPs (AGREE: 18 facts, 22 twinned, 48 patterns, 65 settled). C-007..C-014 need the real engine and build (Q-084) and were not run under the engine TEMP, so whether they hit the same fault is unmeasured. Q-132 records 851 fsa-* scratch dirs already leaked in the user's temp from the same script. Fix shape: reuse TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot's rule (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when GetTempPath() is at or under %SystemRoot%) and record a failed delete instead of throwing. Also grep the other .ps1 under tests/ and eng/ for GetTempPath and $env:TEMP, because rule 2 covers only Core.Tests *.cs.

missed.what: The critique filed M1 on architecture rule 2 and proposed adding `Path\.GetTempPath\s*\(`. It checked only that the rule's patterns matched nothing in Core.Tests today. It never fed the patterns this repo's own path spellings. Pattern 2 needs a `"` straight before the drive letter and pattern 1 needs `)` straight after SpecialFolder.Windows. That lets through `@"\\?\C:\Windows\Temp\..."` (the extended form used in LongPath.ToExtended and TempTree.ExtendedRoot), `Path.Combine(@"C:\", "Windows", "Temp")`, %SystemDrive%\Windows\Temp, and the GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows, SpecialFolderOption.X) overload. A check would be to run the proposed rule over a corpus of each spelling the codebase already uses before calling the class closed.
missed.caught_by: code-review, second adversarial round (R2-M1-2). Waived to SC-177, so rule 2 ships with the holes.

missed.what: The critique's own proposed fix for m2 was incomplete. `\[\s*Trait\s*\(` misses `[Fact, Trait("Network", ...)]` and `[TraitAttribute(...)]`. `Skip\s*=` misses SkipWhen and SkipUnless on data rows. The custom-attribute pattern must also start at `,`, not only `[`, to catch `[Fact, WindowsTempFact]`. The critique did not try its regexes against the bug test's own [WindowsTempFact] or any xUnit v3 skip form.
missed.caught_by: build. The builder found it through corpus rows S05, S18/S19, S23 and S27 and recorded it as a deviation.

missed.what: The design carried 'luafv moves the parent the same way on Windows 10, and in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%' as a must-verify precondition and also filed it for a person. The critique did not ask which stage could discharge it. The answer was none: no Windows 10 machine exists, writing to ProgramData is outside what stages may touch, and Program Files needs an administrator. The obligation was aimed at validate and cost a halted validate #1 and a second lap.
missed.caught_by: validate-slice #1 (halted on O-015); waived to SC-180 only after the lap.

missed.what: The design records 'Only C:\Windows\Temp was measured' and still decides the correction's scope is all of %SystemRoot%, and writes Scanner's class remarks as 'under the Windows folder' in general. The critique did not ask what happens in a writable subfolder of C:\Windows other than Temp where luafv may not move the parent. The correction would under-count there, and the == Facts cover only Temp.
missed.caught_by: code-review, as comment drift only (Scanner.cs:22-26 looser than ScanResult.LastAccessKept). The behavioural scope was not challenged.

unknowns: Does a successful child keep-open move its parent in writable folders under C:\Windows other than Temp (for example Tasks, Tracing, Registration\CRMLog)? Russinovich's quote says luafv excludes 'some specific subdirectories'. The correction fires for all of %SystemRoot% on a structural rule, so if the parent does not move there, kept under-counts. Settle this before Q-159 is reopened for file-age features, because that is when LastAccessKept stops being internal.

Can an administrator confirm with fltmc or a trace that luafv.sys is the component that stamps the parent? So far this rests on correlation with the 'Luaf' pool tag (2 allocations per write-class open, none otherwise). The code is keyed on location, not driver, but the triage doc, the ScanResult remarks and the Scanner remarks all name luafv.

Do the five default-suite Windows-folder Facts stay green on a machine where the user cannot create folders under C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests, or where luafv does not move parents (Windows 10, Q-205)? The Facts assert kept == still-old and never skip, so they would go red on both. Nobody has said whether a red there is the intended signal or an environmental false alarm.
what_went_wrong: Rule 2 was recorded as closed as a class (O-016, a 34-row corpus), but the code review's second adversarial round found six spellings of the Windows Temp folder quiet against it. The finding was waived to SC-177 as 'does not weigh a lap on its own'. The default-suite guard rail therefore ships claiming more than it covers.

Two of the critique's proposed fix patterns (M1, m2) were wrong or incomplete and reached the builder as the fix. The builder had to deviate on rule 1 and the code review found the rule 2 gap. No gate ran the proposed regexes against a corpus first, and critique-review was sized away for this medium, single-designer slice.
validate-slice ran twice. O-015 was aimed at validate although the design had already filed it for a person, and the second pass learned nothing new.

The stale-DLL trap after restoring a mutated file hit twice. Spike 3 threw away three runs (c1-c3). In the build, the bug test and the first full-suite attempt went red spuriously. The design had already recorded the trap as a measured claim, with 'Nothing breaks'.

Loop stages left unrecoverable folders in C:\Windows\Temp: the survey's fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex>, the code review's probable fsa-parity-case-<10 hex>, and validate's two bug-test mutation runs (cleanup unverifiable). All need an administrator.

Five minor findings were waived or carried (SC-173 to SC-177). m7 (SC-174) was then fixed incidentally by the build, so the backlog holds a stale item. The deferred RuleCases finding points at a follow-up slice whose text does not mention RuleCases.
The bug report was only a title. The three build-check criteria were derived from that title, and the only contract was the engine's reproduction test.
